title: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Temporal abstraction in hierarchical world models
abstract: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Temporal hierarchies for long-horizon planning.

units.§1: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] A high-level model predicts over abstract time steps while a low-level model predicts primitive steps.
units.§2: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Reported result. Long-horizon planning return improves with temporal abstraction; prediction error alone did not track planning return.
units.§3: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Limitation. Both levels are trained with separate losses and alternating updates; no solution dependence between levels is modelled.

title: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Bilevel training of latent dynamics
abstract: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Nested optimisation for latent dynamics.

units.§1: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] The upper problem trains a representation; the lower problem fits latent dynamics given the representation.
units.§2: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Method. Hypergradients through the lower-level solution map are approximated with a finite number of inner steps.
units.§3: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Limitation. No planning benchmark is reported; only one-step prediction error.

title: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Multi-loss world-model training with alternating updates

units.§1: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Reconstruction, dynamics and reward losses are minimised by alternating gradient updates.
units.§2: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Claim. Alternating updates are reported to match joint training on the tested tasks.
units.§3: [SYNTHETIC FIXTURE] Scope. Only single-level models were tested.
